title: Anopheles sp midgut dissociation for scRNAseq
author: Silvain Pinaud
materials: Cells are resuspended in 1mL of Sf900III and stained with a combination of Acridine Orange (AO, 318337 from Merck) at 0.5 µg/ml and Ethidium Homodimer-1 (EthD1, E1169 from ThermoFisher) at 1 µg/ml for 5-15’ at 4 °C in the dark. The AO is a cell-permeable fluorescent dye that will emit a green fluorescence at 525 nm when bound to DNA at neutral pH. It was used as a cell-specific marker in our suspension. Meanwhile, EthD1 is a cell-impermeant dye that binds to DNA and emits red fluorescence (617nm). It was used as a counterstain for dying and dead cells in both fluorescent microscopy and FACS in conjunction with the AO.

steps.title: Set up dissociation chamber
steps.instruction: Place the tissue in chambered slides or low‑volume culture plates (capacity < 400 µL) so that the dissociation can be monitored under a microscope throughout the procedure.

steps.title: Prepare dissociation buffer (DB)
steps.instruction: Make 750 µL of DB per well by mixing Sf900III with 10 mg mL⁻¹ Bacillus licheniformis protease and 25 U mL⁻¹ DNase I; keep on ice. Prime pipette tips and needles with DB. Add 200 µL DB to each well, then add three aliquots of 100 µL DB; use the remaining DB for tip priming.

steps.title: Dissect mosquito midguts
steps.instruction: Dissect 10 Anopheles midguts in a droplet of Sf900III, keep the droplet on ice, inspect under a dissection scope for damage or drying, and remove any contaminating tissues.

steps.title: Rinse, cut, and transfer tissue
steps.instruction: Rinse the dissected guts, cut them into small pieces, and transfer them with forceps into a well containing 200 µL DB. Pipette the suspension up and down 30 times with a P1000 (≈2 s up, 2 s down). Start a 90‑minute timer now (the total dissociation must not exceed 90 min).

steps.title: Prime tips and first trituration
steps.instruction: Prime all pipette tips and the needle with DB before use. After 20 min of incubation, mix the tissue suspension 15 times with a P1000 tip primed in DB (≈2 s up, 2 s down).

steps.title: Perform two additional dissociation cycles
steps.instruction: Repeat the following 30‑minute cycle two more times: (1) mix the suspension as above, (2) incubate 20 min, (3) mix again, (4) allow larger tissue pieces to settle for 5 min, then proceed to cell collection.

substeps.instruction: Mix tissue suspension (pipette up/down 15 times, 2 s each direction).
Let larger pieces settle for 5 min.

steps.title: Collect single cells from supernatant
steps.instruction: Gently aspirate 100 µL of supernatant with a primed P200 pipette and transfer it to a 50 mL conical tube that already contains 20 mL Sf900III kept on ice and in the dark.

steps.title: Final tissue processing after 90 min
steps.instruction: Mix the remaining tissue in the chambered slide with 100–200 µL fresh DB using a primed P200 pipette (20 up/down motions, 3 s each) to increase shear force, then transfer the released cells to the same collection tube.

steps.title: Pellet cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the collection tube at 700 g for 5–10 min at 4 °C. Remove the supernatant with a serological pipette without disturbing the pellet (the supernatant may be saved for later checks).

steps.title: Rinse chamber slide
steps.instruction: Rinse the chamber‑slide well with 200 µL cold Sf900III and add the rinse to the same collection tube.

steps.title: Resuspend and filter pellet
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in 200 µL–1.5 mL fresh Sf900III, filter the suspension through a 40 µm mesh (FACS‑compatible), and keep the filtrate on ice (4 °C).

steps.title: Wash cells
steps.instruction: Wash the cells once with cold Sf900III by centrifugation at 500 g, 4 °C. Then perform two additional washes with 1.5 mL Sf900III each, centrifuging at 500 g, 4 °C for 5–10 min per wash.

steps.title: Final resuspension for FACS
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed cells in cold 0.4 % BSA‑Sf900III (FACS‑compatible buffer), keep the tubes on ice and in the dark until sorting or loading for scRNA‑seq.

steps.title: Assess cell concentration and viability
steps.instruction: Determine cell concentration and viability using a fluorescent microscope or automated cell counter. Stain with Acridine Orange (525 nm green) and Ethidium‑Homodimer‑1 (617 nm red) and classify cells as healthy (AO⁺/EthD⁻), dying (AO⁻/EthD⁺), dead (AO⁻/EthD⁺), or high‑quality (well‑defined nucleus, AO⁺/EthD⁻).

steps.title: Store on ice in dark
steps.instruction: Incubate all tubes on ice placed on aluminum foil (≈ ± 4–6 °C) and keep them in the dark until further processing.
